paragraphs: Markets over the last day: the eight tracked equity indices moved -0.27% on average, with Nikkei 225 strongest (+1.94%) and FTSE 100 weakest (-1.68%). Brent crude changed -2.65% to 100.79. Gold changed +0.27% to 4,198.0. Bitcoin changed +0.76% to 84,191.5469. The US 10-year yield stands at 5.241%, a relative move of -0.98%. Among the firms tracked, Santander (-4.45%) and BBVA (-4.16%) moved the most.

Deals and capital markets: Auditor RSM explores IPO to ward off private equity-backed rivals (FT Home). Accounting firm has been sounding out bankers and revamping internal systems to give itself the option of a stock market flotation Deals and capital markets: Boots set to get carved out of private equity (FT Markets). Buyout firm Sycamore is nearing a $9bn deal to sell the chemist to the billionaire Weston family Central banks and macro: Philippines’ central bank braces for ‘Godzilla’ El Niño (FT World). Severe Pacific Ocean weather event could fuel inflationary pressures and hit agricultural production across region Central banks and macro: ECB ‘cannot wait’ for high energy prices to fuel wider inflation, top policymaker warns (FT World). Isabel Schnabel calls for pre-emptive action as price growth accelerates faster than expected in Eurozone’s biggest economies Geopolitics and trade: International Criminal Court cuts ties with Axa over US sanctions (FT World). Move follows fears that broad US sanctions on the war crimes tribunal would force the insurer to cease doing business with it or face punishment
